name: Yuge Sento
description: A serene, airy hospitality theme for a family-run neighbourhood bathhouse (sento), told as one single-column long read through an evening at the bath. Pale tile, misty blue and blue ink with a slate blue used only for numerals, rules and marks; a deeper blue for links and buttons. A slim bar docked at the bottom of the screen holds the Zen Antique Soft wordmark, the menu and today's hours with an Open now / Closed · opens 15:00 / Closed today chip worked out on the server from the site's timezone; on phones it is the wordmark, the chip and a Menu button that opens a full-screen menu read from the bottom up. The home page is a centred reading column: the opening with this evening's hours, five chapters (the curtain, the tiles, the mural, the water, cold milk after) each a short essay and one photograph, a word from the keeper, tonight's prices and the journal, divided by a small three-tile mark. The footer is a tiled waterline over a quiet street plan with the bathhouse marked by its steaming chimney, beside the address card. A faint bath-tile grid texture runs through the bar, the price card and the menu. With An evening, Bath guide (five customs, what to bring), Prices (passes, bring your own), Journal, Newsletter and Visit (a message form that composes an email, no backend). Hours, closed day, address, phone and email are edited once in Appearance > Bath details; the price list is one synced pattern. Zen Antique Soft over Be Vietnam Pro. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
deviation: none for the header, footer and layout codes (H7 / F6 / L7 as planned). Colours as planned (tile #EEF2F5, misty #C9D6E0, blue ink #22323F, slate blue #5F7F96) plus: deep blue #2E5470 for links, buttons, the open chip and small text (7.1:1 on tile, 5.4:1 on misty), quiet slate #4A5A66 for secondary text (6.3:1 on tile, 4.8:1 on misty) and foam #F7F9FB for the price card, the plan and form fields. Blue ink is 11.7:1 on tile and 8.9:1 on misty. Slate blue #5F7F96 is 3.8:1 on tile and 2.9:1 on misty, so it is used only for large display numerals, rules, the three-tile mark, the today marker and the plan's bathhouse mark, never for body text.
